# Portfolio Update

Report 048 | Published 2021-02-21 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2021-2-21/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/048.json)

Curve hedge and position changes.

The report mainly records portfolio actions. Its substantive new issue is the replacement of bills by a multi-factor rate fund, which changes the risk profile even if curve steepening is the intended hedge.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 048-C01

**IVOL hedges curve steepening**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | investment thesis |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | IVOL |
| Source blocks | 8, 12, 15 |
| Thesis family | ivol-curve-hedge |

The fund structure targets curve and volatility exposure, so the intended mechanism is coherent. Replacing bills also adds TIPS duration, option costs and basis risk. A favorable curve move does not guarantee a positive total return.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Business performance and shareholder return are distinct.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Next test:** Measure hedge contribution separately from TIPS returns and compare with the replaced bill allocation.

**Outcome evidence:**

- [IVOL statutory prospectus](https://kraneshares.com/resources/compliance/2022_08_01_quadratic_statutory.prospectus.pdf) | Krane Shares | 2022-08-01 | Verified in the audit

Fund combines TIPS exposure with options tied to interest-rate curve and volatility; total return can differ from any one factor. A steepening benefit is conditional and does not make the fund equivalent to cash.
